prize_parts.citation: for incorporating firm heterogeneity and selection into the analysis of international trade and its gains

statement.case_for: B021 identifies a mature and genuinely transformative research programme. Heterogeneous-firm trade models made selection, productivity dispersion, and reallocation central to trade theory and gave empirical work a coherent framework for studying the distribution and aggregate consequences of globalization. Melitz is indispensable to the canonical framework, while Helpman and Redding represent major complementary theoretical and empirical development. The contribution has endured for more than two decades and is deeply integrated into modern trade research.
statement.case_against: The principal reservation is attribution: the programme builds on a broad lineage in new trade theory and has many important contributors beyond the proposed trio. A citation must therefore remain focused on firm heterogeneity and selection rather than claim credit for all modern quantitative trade research.

responses.point: Friberg judges B021 highly influential but stresses that credit in heterogeneous-firm trade extends beyond three scholars.
responses.response: I agree that the broader literature cannot be compressed without loss. That is precisely why the citation should be narrow: Melitz supplies the defining framework, and Helpman and Redding can be recognized for major linked development rather than as exclusive authors of the entire field.

responses.point: Stromberg gives B018 first place, emphasizing the long-lived practical importance of dynamic-panel GMM while noting misuse and weak-instrument concerns.
responses.response: B018 is an exceptionally mature alternative and its limitations are well characterized, but those limitations also make routine applied influence an imperfect measure of scientific achievement. I place B021 ahead because it changed the central conceptual organization of an entire field while retaining a coherent, if necessarily selective, attribution.

uncertainties: Whether Helpman and Redding are the best two complementary laureates alongside Melitz rather than other major contributors to heterogeneous-firm trade.
How narrowly the citation can delimit the contribution from earlier new-trade theory and subsequent quantitative trade work.
statement.conflict_note: I have long-running collaborations with Peter J. Klenow, a credited name on B050, and would seek recusal from deliberation or voting on that ballot. No connection requiring recusal is apparent from the supplied profile for B021.
